labels.label: def:yamabe-bdry

hypotheses.paper: (Sigma, g) compact Riemannian with boundary, N >= 3
hypotheses.note: the measured model (DEC-139, OQ-44); R_g, H_g are free bounded measurable data of CurvedMetric

hypotheses.paper: EH(Sigma, phi^{4/(N-2)} g) inside the infima eq:relative-yamabe, eq:boundary-yamabe
hypotheses.note: Y_eq_inf_EH / YB_eq_inf_EHB take a family phi -> h phi of metrics with IsConformal and the conformal law (ConformalLaw / ConformalLawB, cited MR1152225, MR1173925) at each competitor; then the strict Y, YB equal the printed infima of EH, EHB
Pos phi and 0 < ||phi||_{L^{p*}} < oo (Adm), resp. on the boundary (AdmB), as in the strict library

findings: l.312-313: EHB divides by Vol(dSigma)^{(N-2)/(N-1)}, so it is undefined for dSigma empty, although l.298 and lem:kobayashi (l.615, 'or dSigma = empty') admit that case; in Lean x/0 = 0. Not a falsity, an unstated n >= 1 for EHB and YB.
questions: l.317-320: the class of conformal factors phi > 0 over which the infima run (smooth, W^{1,2}, positive a.e.?) is not printed. Reading taken: the strict library's Pos (everywhere positive) and Adm/AdmB (finite nonzero L^{p*}, resp. L^{p#}(dSigma), norm).

labels.label: prop:gap-bdry-nonneg

hypotheses.paper: g of constant scalar curvature R_g <= 0
hypotheses.note: weakened to R_g = c vol_g-a.e., c <= 0

hypotheses.paper: sigma^d(Sigma) = sup over conformal classes of Y_[g] (eq:sigma-bdry, l.346-348)
hypotheses.note: sup in EReal of Y over a parameter set C of metrics with g in C (kb/0083); no finiteness needed. Real form: any sigma_b >= Y_[g]

hypotheses.paper: D a space of measurable functions, Sigma compact
hypotheses.note: forall u, AEStronglyMeasurable (val u); IsFiniteMeasure vol_g (as lem_kobayashi_a)

findings: l.358, l.352: sigma^d(Sigma) is a supremum and the paper never states it is finite; prop:gap-bdry-nonneg holds in the extended reals regardless (prop_gap_bdry_nonneg, EReal), but delta is real-valued, as l.352 and eq:accel-bdry treat it, only when sigma^d(Sigma) < +oo.
questions: l.346-348: 'sup over [g]' ranges over the conformal classes of metrics on Sigma; the model cannot define them (R, H free data). Reading taken: a set C of metrics as a parameter, with g in C.

labels.label: prop:accel-bdry

hypotheses.note: AccelLaw at the time t considered, as the dispatch allows; satisfiable (it is linear in rho_i with nonzero coefficient)
one model M, a family g : R -> CurvedMetric X N; a(t) = (Vol(g t)/Vol(g t_i))^{1/N} (l.137); d_tt is deriv (deriv _), the conclusion holds whatever its value
implicit in the paper (a and averages are quotients)
at t only; the non-minimal form needs none
a real sigma_b; the identity holds for every value (kb/0085); the torus form carries sigma_b = 0 (eq:sigma-torus is not this target's label)
real parameters; the matter is not in the model

findings: l.411-414 and Appendix A l.588-594: checked as printed, including the sign of the non-minimal term +2(N-1) int_{dSigma} H bvol/(V_i a^N). The identity is independent of sigma^d: (delta - sigma^d) = -EH, so eq:accel-bdry is eq:accel with <R> = EH/V^{2/N} - 2(N-1)/V int H; it needs sigma^d finite only to be written with delta.

kb_proposals: A supremum of a non-definable invariant (sigma^d) can be stated in EReal over a parameter set C with g in C: the sign statement then needs no boundedness hypothesis (Yamabe.MeasuredModel.sigmaBdry, prop_gap_bdry_nonneg).
Pitfall: iSup_singleton' does not exist at this pin; for (⨆ g ∈ {a}, f g) use simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff, iSup_iSup_eq_left].
notes: Only YamabeScaffold.BoundaryGap rebuilt (nothing upstream moved). The one-line import was appended to scaffold/YamabeScaffold.lean. No new axiom or named external: the conformal law enters as the strict ConformalLaw/ConformalLawB hypotheses, eq:accel as the Prop AccelLaw. Rows are partial only for the model's readings (as lem:kobayashi); no statement is weakened and no row is false as printed.
